text:
maria: heads up — deploy-bot just surfaced a pileup in the rollout approval queue. 12 pending, several are tiny traffic splits during our 23:00-01:00 change window. blocking downstream CI jobs.

deploy-bot: [Automated] 12 rollouts require manual approval. Impact: 8=low (<=1%), 3=medium (1-10%), 1=high (>10%). Queue length increased to 14 in last 10m. See /deploy queue list or logs: https://infralog/redwood/queues/rollouts

jia: ugh, this is the backpressure we talked about. most of those low-impact ones are test toggles and can be fast-tracked. can we add a policy to auto-approve <=1% for internal orgs?

leo: +1 for fast-track but worried about accidental cascades. even 1% on some models caused latency spikes with certain caching patterns. Need a safety check (kv cache warm, model variant ok).

samir: what if we require an automated preflight that runs the canary smoke and a cheap perf probe before allowing auto-approve? like: 
```
# preflight command run by CI
./tools/rollout-preflight --target service:chat-infer --variant v2q --samples 50 --max-latency-ms 200
```
passes => deploy-bot can apply fastpass for that rollout id.

jia: that seems reasonable. we should also add a telemetry tag so we can measure rollback rate for auto-approved splits: `rollout.approval.method=fastpass` and `rollout.impact_bucket=<=1%`.

maria: ops question — can we change the change-window behaviour? current window is strict and approvals outside it get queued even if flagged low-impact. ops wants to avoid extending the window if possible.

opsbot: /suggest extend-window 30m? (automated suggestion based on current backlog)

release-engineering: extending window is a blunt instrument. prefer improving the approval gating so low-impact, preflight-passed rollouts don't touch the queue. two-pronged: 1) implement preflight + fastpass rule, 2) small UI affordance in Console to mark 'auto-approvable' (checkbox) during rollout creation.

leo: what about adding an approval shard for platform team? e.g., requests with tag `platform-managed:true` route to a separate fast lane with shorter SLA for human approval. keeps the main queue safety intact.

samir: that'd be cheap to implement in the router: add `approval_shard` header on rollout creation and have deploy-bot read it. we should also cap rate: no more than 5 fastpass approvals / 10m to avoid burst.

jia: agree on rate cap. also add a config whitelist for owners/orgs allowed to request fastpass. otherwise someone could abuse internal scripts.

maria: sounds like consensus. action items: 
- samir: spike preflight runner + deploy-bot hook (ETA 3d)
- jia: telemetry/event schema + console flag design (ETA 2d)
- leo: draft safety checklist for preflight smoke (co-own with infra) (ETA 1d)
- release-engineering: small console UX (checkbox + tooltip) (ETA 4d)

deploy-bot: [Automated] Marking thread with tag `deploy:approval-backpressure`. If anything is urgent, use `/deploy approve <id> --manual`. Example: `/deploy approve 1801456901 --note "fastpass-by-maria"`.

maria: I'll manually approve the 3 truly time-sensitive ones now. others we let the pipeline handle after the preflight feature lands. :thumbsup:

leo: one more ask — can we emit an alert when approval latency > 10m for >5 rollouts? want to catch this earlier.

jia: will add an alert rule to telemetry: `alert.rollout.approval.latency` with severity=page if >20 pending and avg latency > 10m.

release-engineering: ok locking this in. I'll create a tracking ticket and put the PR checklist in the ticket. referencing this thread.

maria: thanks all. updating the change window is off the table for now unless the alert fires.

opsbot: /note Change-window unchanged. Monitoring threshold set.

samir: assigning myself a spike item now. will post updates in this thread.

maria: thanks — keep updates here.
